learning_objective: 🎯 Learn a hard lesson about greed and vanity! See how borrowing a single piece of jewelry ruins a woman's entire life.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Matilda Loisel is pretty but born into a poor family and married to a simple clerk. She constantly daydreams of luxury, rich food, and beautiful dresses, making herself miserable.
Her husband brings an invitation to a grand Ministerial ball. Instead of being happy, she cries because she has no dress. Her husband gives her his savings (400 francs) to buy a dress.
Still unhappy without jewelry, Matilda borrows a beautiful 'diamond' necklace from her rich friend, Mme Forestier. She is the star of the party, but loses the necklace on her way home!

Instead of telling the truth, the Loisels buy a replacement real diamond necklace for 36,000 francs. They take huge loans. For 10 years, Matilda works extremely hard, washing dishes and scrubbing floors to pay off the debt. She loses all her beauty.
After 10 years, she meets Mme Forestier and tells her everything. Mme Forestier is shocked and reveals that the original borrowed necklace was fake (imitation), worth only 500 francs!

fun_activity.title: 🗣️ The Power of Truth
fun_activity.instructions: Imagine you are Matilda the morning after losing the necklace. Write a 2-line text message to Mme Forestier telling her the truth. How different would Matilda's life be if she sent that text?

exam_tips: 📌 Contrast Matilda's nature (dreamy, greedy) with her husband's nature (practical, loving, self-sacrificing).
📌 Discuss 'The Necklace' as a symbol of human vanity and fake social status.
📌 Explain how suffering and hard work completely transformed Matilda's physical appearance and attitude.
quick_recap: ⭐ The story is written by Guy de Maupassant.
⭐ Mr. Loisel sacrificed the money he saved to buy a gun for hunting, just to buy Matilda a dress.
⭐ A single lie and the fear of social embarrassment destroyed ten years of two lives.
